text:
maya (AE): Heads-up: Prospect 'Sentinel Systems' sent a POC checklist. Main concerns: output parity vs CompetitorX, streaming chunk behavior, and their security questionnaire. Can we triage quickly?

noah (SE): Copy. Ask them to share the exact CompetitorX request/response pairs they used. Most deltas come from model id/temperature and tokenization differences.

maya (AE): Pasted sample below (redacted):
```
POST https://api.competitorx.com/v1/completions
{ "prompt": "Summarize:\n- user: loved the feature...", "max_tokens": 120 }
// they show completion_tokens: 38 and a terser phrasing
```
They say when they hit us the token count is +10 and wording is more verbose.

lina (Security): high level on questionnaire: they require SOC2 (in-rotation ok), customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), VPC peering or dedicated private, and log retention 12+ months. Also want to run a narrow pentest against the POC.

noah (SE): Action items I see: (1) provide a small compatibility shim mapping CompetitorX envelope to our API so their client can swap endpoints with minimal change; (2) produce token mapping report and token-normalized billing view; (3) enable low-latency streaming mode to mimic CompetitorX chunk sizes for client validation.

owen (Infra): streaming note: our default minimizes RPCs and batches tokens into larger frames. We have a runtime flag streaming.chunk_target_bytes that can be reduced for the POC. Will need an infra change on the poc cluster.

maya (AE): Procurement ask: can we give a short-term reserved price for a 6-week POC? They prefer committed capacity for consistent latency.

oehn (typo)
noah (SE): typo in channel — meant to say: we can propose a short reserved offer: 6-week minimum on a small Dedicated pool (single GPU equivalent) + burst to 2 nodes. I'll sketch numbers after infra confirms resource footprint.

lina (Security): For pentest coordination, I need a contact who can approve attack windows and a scope doc limiting tests to the POC environment. Who owns that?

owen (Infra): I'll own pentest coordination. We'll create a temporary POC VPC and schedule tests during off-peak. Need their test IPs and list of endpoints.

maya (AE): I'll request the CompetitorX request logs, their staging IPs, and their target region (they asked about EU data residency).

noah (SE): For prompt parity: provide them with two quick paths: (A) client-side shim that rewrites request envelope and normalizes whitespace/tokenization before sending to Redwood; (B) server-side compatibility layer we can run in the POC which rewrites responses to match token accounting and chunk sizes. Shim example: 
```
# shim (bash)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-lite","input":"Summarize:\n- user: loved the feature...","max_output_tokens":120}'
```
This also lets us instrument token counts pre/post.

lina (Security): Quick answers: SOC2 report available (we can provide the auditor letter), AWS KMS support for Private/CMEK, SSO via SAML, VPC peering/dedicated supported. Will prepare completed questionnaire and attach SOC2 artifact.

maya (AE): timeline: they want a demo next Wednesday and to spin a 4-week POC immediately after.

owen (Infra): devops-bot: provisioning poc-sentinel-1 in eu-west-1 with streaming.chunk_target_bytes=8kb (low-latency).

devops-bot: Provisioned poc-sentinel-1 (eu-west-1). streaming.chunk_target_bytes=8192.

maya (AE): :thumbsup: Noah, can you prepare the shim + a side-by-side harness so they can compare CompetitorX vs Redwood outputs? Keep it minimal.

noah (SE): On it. I'll deliver: adapter script, token-mapping table, and an eval harness with their sample prompts by EOD Friday. If parity still off, we can propose a minor tuning or temperature/frequency penalty adjustments as optional line item.

lina (Security): I'll return the questionnaire by EOD Monday. Also need the legal vendor name for the contract routing.

maya (AE): I'll DM legal vendor name and the staging IPs to Owen.

noah (SE): Note: we should expose both raw token counts and normalized counts in the Console during the POC so procurement can reconcile billing with CompetitorX. I'll add that to the deliverables.

owen (Infra): Confirmed. Also set up IP allowlist and a temporary audit-log retention of 13 months on the POC cluster.

maya (AE): Great team. Next steps: Noah - shim + harness by Fri; Lina - questionnaire + SOC2 artifact by Mon; Owen - VPC/IP prep and pentest windows; Maya - pricing proposal and demo scheduling.

noah (SE): Will also include a brief note on expected tokenization differences and a conversion heuristic to explain the +10 tokens they observed.

maya (AE): Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the prospect and share the demo invite.
